title: Power Automate for desktop: flowchart mode for building and viewing desktop flows
summary: Hold for an unsupported restriction on switching back to sequence mode. Microsoft documents the no-errors prerequisite for switching into flowchart mode, but the briefing applies it to both directions. The roadmap facts, maker controls and surrounding licensing statements are otherwise supported.

claims.claim: Flowchart mode is a visual authoring mode for building and viewing desktop flows in Power Automate for desktop.
claims.quote: Flowchart mode provides a visual authoring experience in which desktop flow actions are represented as nodes and the connections between nodes are represented as edges.

claims.claim: Actions appear as nodes on a canvas.
claims.quote: Flowchart mode displays actions as connected nodes on a canvas.

claims.claim: Edges between nodes show execution paths.
claims.quote: Each action is represented as a node, and edges connect the nodes to show their execution paths.

claims.claim: Microsoft says this view can make branches, loops and complex execution paths easier to understand.
claims.quote: This view can make execution paths easier to understand, especially in flows that contain branches, loops, or other complex logic.

claims.claim: Both modes represent the same desktop flow.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance

claims.quote: A loop node has a loop-back edge that represents the loop body and an outgoing edge that continues execution after the loop finishes.

claims.claim: Node indexes in flowchart mode match action indexes in sequence mode.
claims.quote: Node index badges match the action indexes you see in sequence mode.

claims.claim: The documented change concerns visualizing and editing the same flow rather than introducing a separate runtime.
claims.quote: Both modes represent the same desktop flow. Flowchart mode changes how you visualize and edit the current subflow. You still have access to other designer capabilities.

claims.claim: Move and Reorder use different keyboard shortcuts.
claims.quote: The Ctrl+Shift+Arrow shortcuts change only the node's position on the canvas. The Shift+Alt+Arrow shortcuts change the flow's execution order.
